purpose: Recommendations and proposed implementations for the owner integration agent; independent evaluation precedes any integration.

integration_protocol.first_action: Confirm the target repository and compare current main with the pinned base; reconcile intervening changes before evaluating any patch.
integration_protocol.work_state: patches; repository runtime files on the handoff branch remain at the base
integration_protocol.application: Extract the listed patch files, verify their SHA-256 values, and apply selected patches to a separate integration worktree. Do not merge the .reference payload into main as implementation.
integration_protocol.independence: Each patch is based independently on the pinned base. The manifest also records the ordered combined evaluation tree. Acceptance may be per patch or adapted implementation.
integration_protocol.test_imports: Select the integration worktree explicitly through its environment/PYTHONPATH. Reusing an editable installation can silently import the original source checkout.
integration_protocol.checkout_regression: For GJ-RC-06, make a disposable evaluation commit before running repository tests because the byte comparison intentionally reads HEAD.
integration_protocol.gates: Run relevant installed-package and qualified browser/deployment CI on the actual integration SHA. Green local source-tree checks and Proffer validation do not grant acceptance or publication authority.
integration_protocol.disposition: In the owning issue, record the immutable handoff SHA, reused/adapted/deferred/rejected concern IDs, actual integration SHA when applicable, check sources and next trigger for any deferred item. Use Proffer disposition records; producer does not claim consumer acceptance.

recommended_sequence.gate: Resolve remaining HTTPS credential policy before freezing accepted v1 input.
Shared-bucket collection apply remains gated until private roots and maintenance fencing are qualified.
Freeze accepted historical bytes once; consume them with later installed builds.

concerns.title: Bind verification to the selected signature family
concerns.finding: Git's gpg.format is a signing default; it does not force verify-commit to use that family. A valid OpenPGP commit in an ambient trusted keyring can satisfy the existing SSH path even when the supplied SSH allowed-signers file is unrelated.
concerns.impact: The recorded external SSH authority can differ from the authority that actually verified the edition. A wrong-family signature also selects a verifier backend outside the expected pinning path.

steps: Inspect the raw immutable commit object with replacements disabled before invoking Git signature verification.
Recognize one unambiguous SSH or OpenPGP gpgsig header and require the selected family to match the caller-provided independent policy.
Retain the existing pinned executable, cryptographic verification, full GPG fingerprint or external SSH allowed-signers checks.
Use an offline frozen real OpenPGP commit/public key fixture to prove ambient GPG trust cannot satisfy an SSH policy; retain real SSH and tampering cases.

acceptance: Matching SSH and explicit OpenPGP policies verify real valid signatures.
Wrong-family, duplicate, unsupported and malformed signatures fail before any verifier backend executes.
Matching armor with altered signed bytes still fails cryptographic verification.
Run publication/discovery contracts and inspect direct trusted_git callers for acceptance changes.
limitations_and_decisions: The proposed 64 KiB whole-commit bound matches the existing publication_protocol limit; it newly applies that restriction to direct trusted_git callers. Review whether to share the limit instead of duplicating it.
Exact armor and single-gpgsig requirements reject alternate signature headers, including gpgsig-sha256; existing publication IDs remain SHA-1. Confirm the intended v1 acceptance contract.
The new fixture verifies a public historical Git object with only its public key. It is not a full frozen GuavaJam publication corpus.
Object inspection adds two Git subprocesses per verification; no performance claim is made.

evidence.supports: Verification selects trust settings but does not inspect the signature family.
Existing publication commit-object limits and durable input shape.
Git chooses the verification format from signature data; this moving upstream source is explanatory, while the regression is the pinned repository evidence.

concerns.title: Preserve source-approved external links across historical rendering
concerns.finding: Core accepts mailto links with query parameters, but the renderer rejects them. A later edit removing the link does not repair regeneration of the retained earlier edition.
concerns.impact: A valid signed source history can be discoverable yet impossible for the generator to rebuild.

steps: Consult the core valid_source_link contract for external-link syntax and preserve source-approved mailto queries.
Continue to enforce generator-owned image origin restrictions and credential-bearing URL refusal.
Exercise a real signed two-edition history with mailto queries in both manuscript and supporting GFM; rebuild it after the later edition removes the links.
Before freezing v1, choose and document a shared policy for credential-bearing HTTPS links, which core currently accepts and the renderer refuses. Inspect retained source before any tightening.

acceptance: The earlier edition and its exact mailto query targets render after a later correction.
Malformed HTTPS authority is rejected consistently.
Credential rejection and image-origin checks remain covered.
Do not mark complete URI parity achieved until the credential-policy decision and historical-source consequences are tested.
limitations_and_decisions: The patch deliberately leaves the credential-bearing HTTPS mismatch visible in a regression test; it fixes the demonstrated mailto/history defect, not every policy difference.
A blanket stricter validator would invalidate old signed sources. Resolve syntax in core and rendering capability deliberately, without silently reinterpreting accepted history.

evidence.supports: valid_source_link permits mailto query parameters and credential-bearing HTTPS.
_href independently rejects mailto queries and URL credentials.

concerns.title: Protect private authoring roots before shared-bucket collection apply
concerns.priority: P1 when shared-bucket deletion is in scope
concerns.finding: The retained-asset scan sees public remote roots plus the collector checkout. Staged assets referenced only by another active private clone can outlive their upload lease and become collection candidates.
concerns.impact: A manual shared-bucket sweep can delete bytes still needed by private work.

steps: Keep collection planning available; establish an explicit v1 operational gate for shared-bucket apply until private-root completeness and writer coordination are qualified.
Separate durable registration and explicit retirement of private roots from short-lived per-asset upload leases.
Use exact immutable source snapshots and independent root authority; unavailable, stale or invalid active roots must block deletion instead of silently disappearing.
Preserve reader-only preview credentials and separate authority for registration/renewal and deletion.
Require a bucket-wide maintenance window that actually fences all relevant writers/reference-adoption workflows, or implement a genuine shared fencing protocol before permitting concurrent operation.

acceptance: Two independent private clones retain their referenced assets beyond the upload grace period.
Expired, unreachable, stale or corrupt active private authorities cause apply to refuse deletion.
Retirement is explicit and cannot remove permanent protection for released assets.
Concurrent renewal, adoption, upload and collection are tested at phase boundaries, including a resumed stale process.
Inventory changes still abort apply; no local lock or last-moment read is represented as a distributed fence.
limitations_and_decisions: No collector patch is supplied because safe authority/retirement/fencing semantics require a concrete owner decision.

The current operator_lock is checkout-local. Existing collect documentation assumes writers and reference changes are paused throughout the sweep; rechecking immediately before deletion alone leaves a race.
The detailed design offers a bounded v1 gate as an alternative to rushing a new distributed retention protocol.

evidence.supports: Existing owner-tracked private-root protection requirement.
Local operator lock, collection grace period and inventory rechecks.
retained_assets enumerates remote and collector-local source roots.

concerns.title: Restore the last-good private preview after replacement failure
concerns.finding: Refresh stops the current listener before replacement startup/readiness succeeds. Replacement failure can leave the old output on disk with no listener serving it.
concerns.impact: A failed preview refresh makes an otherwise valid private workspace unavailable and can leave a child process holding the port.

steps: Retain accepted output, manifest, revision and reader configuration until candidate readiness succeeds.
On spawn/early-exit/readiness failure, stop and reap the candidate, restart the last-good listener, and keep the refresh error visible through failed service health.
Delete output only after its owning process is stopped. If restoration fails, retain accepted files and state for retry.
Reap already-exited children and escalate graceful-shutdown timeout to bounded kill/wait.

acceptance: Inject spawn failure, early child exit and readiness timeout; the old revision remains available when rollback succeeds.
A later retry replaces the preview successfully.
Failed rollback retains accepted state and files and exposes failure.
Candidate files are never removed while its process remains active; shutdown timeout is bounded.
limitations_and_decisions: Rollback can briefly interrupt connections and depends on the old listener being restartable.
Readiness remains an authenticated root-page check, not a guarantee that every asset/provider is healthy.
Reused in-memory reader credentials may have been externally revoked. No browser/Compose/live-provider run was repeated for this patch.

evidence.supports: Replacement startup and process/output lifecycle.

concerns.title: Fail closed when private extractor output custody is uncertain
concerns.finding: The review-output guard treats most failed Git discovery results as evidence of being outside a worktree. Inherited GIT_* routing variables can also hide or redirect discovery.
concerns.impact: Private extracted conversation text can be written inside a repository when the guard cannot establish its location.

steps: Resolve the existing output parent and refuse a .git marker at any ancestor, including linked worktrees.
Run Git discovery with inherited GIT_* variables removed, C locale and cross-filesystem discovery enabled.
Accept only a recognized outside-worktree response; fail on timeout, execution/config/ownership errors or unexpected output.
Retain exclusive file creation and 0600 private output permissions.

acceptance: Normal external output succeeds and repository/linked-worktree output is refused.
GIT_DIR, GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES and config routing cannot change custody decisions.
Timeout, dubious ownership, bad config, missing/unexpected replies refuse output without creating a file.
Qualify the exact outside-repository diagnostic under every supported Git/OS baseline.
limitations_and_decisions: The reference recognizes an exact C-locale Git diagnostic tested with Git 2.56.1. Other diagnostics fail closed and can require portability adaptation.
Bare-repository policy is unchanged: an explicit false worktree response is accepted.
This is not a hostile-filesystem race or malicious-local-user security boundary.

evidence.supports: review_output_path accepts nonzero discovery status too broadly.

concerns.title: Stabilize tracked runtime checkout bytes used in renderer identity
concerns.finding: Checkout line-ending conversion changes renderer fingerprints. Extending draft PR #79 to all tracked runtime inputs reproduced 15 drifting text files, beyond its six JavaScript files.
concerns.impact: The same commit can produce different renderer identities and unnecessary or inconsistent rebuild decisions across checkouts.

steps: Set text=auto eol=lf at both core and generator runtime package roots whose bytes feed renderer_identity.
Reuse PR #79 test_renderer_checkout.py, broadening its tracked-input set to all files in those roots while retaining explicit JavaScript coverage.
Use a temporary index and compare committed file bytes after false, input and true core.autocrlf checkouts. Preserve binary auto-detection.

acceptance: All tracked hashed runtime bytes match across all three autocrlf modes.
Binary assets retain their original bytes.
Run the regression from a disposable commit containing the patch because it intentionally inspects HEAD.
limitations_and_decisions: Linux Git checkout-mode simulation passed; native Windows qualification remains separate.
This changes runtime checkout normalization and may intentionally cause one renderer-identity transition; it does not change signed source identities.
Reconcile with PR #79 rather than creating two competing copies of the regression.

evidence.supports: Existing draft checkout-byte regression; inspected head 1ccb4443ab10dac1405358b30f0746c9914af054.
renderer_identity hashes both runtime package roots.
Existing per-suffix normalization misses hashed runtime resources.

concerns.title: Pin the first documented initializer to the reviewed revision
concerns.finding: The first README initializer runs an unpinned Git URL even though subsequent setup is expected to use a reviewed tool reference.
concerns.impact: A user can bootstrap with different code from the revision they reviewed or subsequently configure.

steps: Add @<reviewed-sha> to the work initializer and align the instructions with GUAVAJAM_TOOL_REF.
Check both README initializer examples and matching revisions where an example uses multiple packages.

acceptance: Both documented initializer commands pin each executed package.
The repository documentation/link policy still passes.
limitations_and_decisions: The placeholder must be replaced with a reviewed immutable revision by the operator; this patch does not choose a release SHA.

evidence.supports: First initializer is unpinned; later index initializer already uses a reviewed reference.

concerns.title: Define a coordinated RC version mapping and exact artifact names
concerns.priority: P2: decide before producing an RC
concerns.finding: Root release tooling accepts only numeric x.y.z and coordinates identical version strings, while Python prereleases, extension package SemVer and Chrome manifest numeric versions have different representations.
concerns.impact: A real 1.0.0rc1 cannot be prepared through the existing coordinated path. A naive fourth-component candidate version can sort after a shorter final version.

steps: Use canonical Python-style M.m.prcN as the coordinated RC identity; derive extension M.m.p-rc.N and Chrome M.m.p.N.
Reserve Chrome fourth component 65535 for final and restrict RC numbers to 1..65534; use version_name for the human-readable SemVer.
Keep extension mapping validation in extension-owned tools so its standalone build remains independent.
Select exact expected artifact filenames per ecosystem in an empty release output directory; prefix globbing must not confuse rc1 with stale rc10.
Preserve prepare-release as artifact preparation with no automatic tags, registry upload or publication.

acceptance: Check rc1 < rc2 < final < next patch rc1 for Chrome, and correct prerelease ordering for Python/SemVer.
Reject unsupported suffixes, leading zeroes and out-of-range components.
Build/install all RC Python distributions, load the independently built extension under the qualified Chrome baseline, and test installed handoff.
Record per-artifact version, exact source SHA and checksums; reject stale artifacts.
limitations_and_decisions: The proposed final Chrome version is 1.0.0.65535, with version_name 1.0.0. Owner acceptance is required before adopting this durable mapping.
No version bump, lockfile update, release or new RC artifact is included in this handoff.

evidence.supports: Current numeric-only coordinated version parser.
Current manifest/package equality and independent extension build.
Chrome numeric component constraints and ordering.

concerns.title: Make existing CI checks enforceable for stabilization
concerns.finding: The inspected main branch reports protected=false, required-check enforcement off and no repository rulesets, despite a successful existing seven-job CI run.
concerns.impact: Passing CI is not currently an enforced condition for changing the stabilization source or promoting an artifact.

steps: Re-read current settings and configure an active ruleset for main and any explicitly selected stabilization branch.
Require the seven observed check-run contexts tied to GitHub Actions integration 15368, PRs, current-base checks, and no deletion/non-fast-forward updates.
Choose review count and emergency bypass deliberately for the actual maintainer model.
If adopting a merge queue, add and qualify merge_group triggers first.
Promote only the exact immutable source SHA whose required checks succeeded; treat tag protection/publication authority as a separate release action.

acceptance: Read back the rules and exact required contexts.
Qualify passing and intentionally failing disposable PRs through the intended path without rewriting main.
Confirm promotion metadata refers to the checked source SHA and immutable artifact hashes.
limitations_and_decisions: API observations are time-bound; reconcile later owner changes rather than overwriting them.
This handoff provides an actionable settings proposal, not evidence that protections are already enabled.
The existing CI includes browser, Compose/local S3, licensing, package isolation and installed archive handoff; the recommendation is to enforce those existing gates.

evidence.supports: Observed unprotected main at the reviewed commit.
Observed empty ruleset list.
Successful baseline CI on the reviewed commit; not a run of these reference patches.

concerns.title: Freeze real historical artifacts as the v1 compatibility gate
concerns.priority: P2: establish before finalizing the RC contract
concerns.finding: Namespace checks and current-producer/current-consumer tests do not by themselves preserve the ability to read previously accepted signed source, archives, catalogs or continuity state.
concerns.impact: A coordinated implementation change can make both ends of a test agree while silently breaking older durable artifacts.

steps: After accepting the RC source/authority contract, create a synthetic immutable corpus once, with exact byte hashes and producer versions.
Preserve a signed two-edition bundle/public trust, source archive and tiny asset, catalog/checkpoint/feed continuity, native branching archive, and expected canonical citations.
Have later installed core, generator and extractor artifacts consume the frozen inputs in their owning test lanes.
Keep durable source/citations/accepted-history distinct from rebuildable renderer/search/cache output.
Add new corpus versions without regenerating or replacing earlier accepted fixtures; fail unknown schema versions non-destructively.

acceptance: Verify fixture hashes before opening them.
Consume old inputs from clean installed artifacts outside the checkout.
Preserve canonical commit/path/anchor citations, accepted edition order and feed identity.
Tampered/unknown inputs fail without replacing last-good authority or state.
No ordinary test invocation regenerates the frozen corpus with current producer code.
limitations_and_decisions: The proposed promise is backward reading of selected v1-RC durable artifacts through v1.x, subject to owner acceptance.
Future-feature acceptance by old binaries is a separate forward-compatibility decision.
No complete compatibility corpus is frozen here; do that after the authority fixes and RC identity are accepted.

evidence.supports: Existing namespace contracts are distinct from historical byte compatibility.
Existing installed-artifact lane can host durable-input compatibility checks.
Existing independent archive/extractor installed handoff boundary.

concerns.title: Align the deployment example release authority with runtime keys
concerns.finding: The deploy identity example grants writes beneath sha256/.released, while the actual release namespace and generated policy use released/sha256. The nearby Compose environment comment describes the stale namespace too.
concerns.impact: An operator following the example can provision a release credential that cannot write the runtime release records.

steps: Use the existing runtime release prefix in the example credential policy and accompanying environment comment; align both Read and Write grants with the generated release role.
Cross-check the example release grant against the generated role policy and canonical runtime prefix in a deployment configuration regression.

acceptance: The release example authorizes the same prefix as the generated release-writer policy.
Private asset/pin authority stays separate from public release-record authority.
Deployment configuration and repository contracts pass.
limitations_and_decisions: This corrects example setup; it does not migrate an existing provider credential or perform a live release.

evidence.supports: Stale release-writer prefix in checked-in provisioning example.
Stale descriptive release namespace.
Canonical RELEASE_PREFIX used by runtime.

additional_observations.observation: The signature-format cap is newly enforced for direct trusted_git callers but already exists for normal publication verification; avoid presenting it as a newly lowered publication limit.
The shared helper also rejects malformed HTTPS authority that the old renderer could emit; credential-bearing HTTPS remains a conscious unresolved policy difference.
Local operator locking plus inventory rechecks do not serialize multiple private clones or a resumed writer across a collector sweep.
Graceful shutdown timeout could leave the Node process holding the listener port; the patch adds bounded kill/reap.
The complete hashed corpus shows 15 CRLF drifts, including nine non-JavaScript text resources.
Artifact prefix matching can confuse rc1 and stale rc10; exact filenames and a clean per-release output directory belong in the RC implementation.
Stale example release-writer authority was discovered during the private-retention review.

existing_owner_scope.treatment: Preserve the existing private-retention issue as the implementation owner; the new handoff issue coordinates evaluation.
Reuse/adapt its checkout regression; no merge or closure performed by this handoff.
Spoken screen-reader qualification is explicitly deferred by the owner; it is not promoted to a new RC blocker here.
